governing: seat_flexure: flexural yielding of the seat angle's outstanding leg at its critical section (Manual Part 10), 5.917 kip-in demand against 6.315 kip-in allowable
notes: Petra check of this exact design (try4.petra) prints PASS: 14 obligations, all certified, ASD, shear 0 to 15.843 kip. Seat: L5x3-1/2x3/8, 6 in long, 3-1/2 in leg under the beam, 1/2 in setback. The seat angle must be A572 Gr 50. In A36 the same angle fails seat flexure at 1.30, so do not substitute A36. Four 3/4 in A325-N bolts (group 120, threads included, snug, standard holes) in 2 rows at 3-1/2 in gauge through the W10x49 web. The top row is 1-3/4 in below the heel and the pitch is 2-1/4 in. That leaves 1 in from the bottom bolt to the toe, exactly the Table J3.4 minimum. Petra does not check that toe edge distance or bolt-head room under the outstanding leg; I checked both by hand: the head clears the 3/8 in leg and its fillet. Top angle L4x4x1/4 A36 is for stability only, and Petra does not design its bolts. Next-closest checks: spacing_min 0.889, bottom hole within the vertical leg (web_fit) 0.881, web crippling 0.677. Petra's report lists the modes it does not check. Two of them are the top angle's flexibility (rotation) and any local effects in the W10x49 web beyond the bolt bearing. The 3/8 in critical-section offset in the seat flexure model is a judged premise, recalled from the Manual rather than checked against its text.
